evidence.claim: AMLO announced a five-year world truce proposal that would suspend military actions, nuclear tests, and missile tests and create a mediation committee for Ukraine.
evidence.title: Discurso del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador durante el desfile cívico militar: 212 Aniversario de la Independencia
evidence.excerpt: AMLO announced a five-year world truce proposal that would suspend military actions, nuclear tests, and missile tests and create a mediation committee for Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential transcript with date and first-person ruler statement.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler-period statement with precise date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct AMLO statement and proposal; the foreign ministry was assigned to present it at the UN.
contrary_evidence: It is a proposal rather than an implemented policy or treaty.
It does not show command over nuclear forces because Mexico has none.

evidence.claim: Mexico called for a security perimeter around Zaporizhzhia and a demilitarized zone so IAEA inspections could proceed safely.
evidence.title: Common Sense, Cooperation Must Guide Way Forward towards Ensuring Safety of Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Secretary-General Tells Security Council
evidence.excerpt: Mexico called for a security perimeter around Zaporizhzhia and a demilitarized zone so IAEA inspections could proceed safely.
evidence.source_locator: Mexico statement in the Security Council briefing on Zaporizhzhia
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN Security Council meeting coverage with attributed national intervention.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year and tied to the Zaporizhzhia crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN mission; relevant to AMLO only as foreign-policy posture, not personal nuclear command.
contrary_evidence: This addresses a foreign crisis, not Mexico's own nuclear command-and-control.
It is diplomatic advocacy, not an operational safety action inside Mexico.

evidence.claim: Mexico warned that a nuclear accident at Zaporizhzhia would have unacceptable humanitarian and environmental consequences and called for a security perimeter around the plant.
evidence.title: Fighting at Ukraine Nuclear Power Site Irresponsible, against Geneva Conventions, Under-Secretary-General Tells Security Council
evidence.excerpt: Mexico warned that a nuclear accident at Zaporizhzhia would have unacceptable humanitarian and environmental consequences and called for a security perimeter around the plant.

contrary_evidence: The evidence concerns a crisis abroad, not Mexican nuclear infrastructure.
It does not demonstrate internal command-and-control reform.

evidence.claim: AMLO sent a message to a forum focused on justice, non-intervention, peaceful settlement, and humanitarian aid for people affected by the war in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Llamado del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador a la paz

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential site with ruler-authored message and target-date context.
contrary_evidence: This is a public statement, not a demonstrated policy outcome.
It does not show operational leverage over the war.

evidence.claim: Mexico said it had negotiated a balanced humanitarian draft with France, abstained on the Russian draft because it lacked Article 2.4 and an unequivocal cessation of hostilities, and prioritized humanitarian action, civilian protection, and international humanitarian law.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN mission and foreign ministry.
contrary_evidence: Abstention can be read as cautious legalism rather than maximal pressure.

evidence.claim: Mexico said it supported impartial investigations, the ICC and ICJ processes, and that even in war all channels should be maintained for dialogue with Russian authorities.
evidence.title: General Assembly Adopts Text to Suspend Russian Federation from Human Rights Council, Continuing Emergency Special Session on Humanitarian Crisis in Ukraine

evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 period fit and relevant to crisis diplomacy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN delegation.
contrary_evidence: Abstaining on suspension is a softer posture than maximal isolation.
It does not itself end or prevent the war.

evidence.claim: Mexico said the occupied-territory referendums had no validity under international law, supported Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, supported Secretary-General-led diplomacy, and voted in favour of the resolution.
evidence.title: With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation’s Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions

evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN delegation.
contrary_evidence: Voting for a resolution is not the same as stopping annexation or war.
This is still diplomatic/legal conduct, not battlefield conduct.

evidence.claim: Canada, Mexico, and the United States reaffirmed support for Ukraine’s independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, condemned Russia’s invasion, called for humanitarian relief, and described a diplomatic path forward.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution through Mexico's foreign ministry.
contrary_evidence: This is negotiated multilateral language, not a unilateral presidential order.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 evidence on AMLO's personal control over civilian-nuclear safety appointments, regulatory discipline, or command-side decisions is thin.
There is no Mexico-originating war, proxy conflict, or coercive peace leverage in 2022, so the dossier is mostly diplomatic posture rather than operational conflict conduct.
Specific chain-of-command evidence for some police, military, and intelligence abuses remains incomplete, especially for local versus federal responsibility.
Some of the evidence about electoral reform and media pressure is rhetorical or journalistic rather than a direct legal finding of intent to entrench power.
The causal split between AMLO policy, inherited weakness, and global shocks is still only partially recoverable for 2022 poverty, inflation, and investment outcomes.
Independent post-launch quality and outcome audits for IMSS-Bienestar, education recovery, and related welfare programs are thinner than the rollout record.
Direct documentary evidence of personal enrichment, hidden financial benefit, or knowing approval of surveillance remains limited.
Durability and post-launch independent audits for AIFA, Dos Bocas, IMSS-Bienestar, and the education programs are thinner than the implementation record.
